- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract downward momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values to reduce noise.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates downward drift in low-sentiment periods; apply 1–3% upward bias to offset mean reversion bias.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is near historical highs, model often overestimates continuation; reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect potential pullback.
